finding.claim: Blind SSRF: a subscriber-supplied callbackUrl is stored without validation and the server later sends an outbound HTTP POST to it every minute via notifyAll, so an attacker can make the service POST to arbitrary http/https destinations, including internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints. The response is discarded, so the attacker gets no response data, only side effects and timing.
finding.source: src/Jobs.java:13-14 subscribe(name, callbackUrl) stores the caller-supplied callbackUrl in the static subscriptions map. The comment at line 12 says it comes from the POST /subscribe body. No validation is applied.
finding.sink: src/Jobs.java:21 URI.create(cb) and src/Jobs.java:24 client.send(req, ...) inside notifyAll, which POSTs the payload to every stored callback URL.

trace.note: Comment documents POST /subscribe with body fields name and callbackUrl. This is the untrusted entry point. No auth check is visible in this file.
subscribe(String name, String callbackUrl) receives the attacker-controlled URL.
subscriptions.put(name, callbackUrl) persists it with no scheme, host, IP, or length check.
notifyAll iterates all stored callback values; the scheduler runs it every minute.
URI.create(cb) parses the stored string. There is no re-validation and no rebuild from parsed components.
Builds a POST with a server-chosen payload body. The attacker does not control the body here.
client.send issues the request from the server's network position. The response body is discarded, so the attack is blind.

finding.guards_checked: None on the path. subscribe() does no validation. notifyAll() does no allowlist, blocklist, DNS or IP check, and no scheme check of its own. Incidental limits, not security controls: java.net.http only accepts http/https URIs, so file:, ftp: and gopher: are rejected. HttpClient.newHttpClient() uses the default redirect policy (NEVER), so redirects cannot pivot to internal hosts. Host is not constrained, so the full SSRF surface applies.

verdict.guard_found: none in src/Jobs.java: subscribe() at line 13-14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated, and notifyAll() at lines 19-24 applies no host, scheme, or IP check before client.send. Redirects are off by default, so no redirect pivot.
verdict.reason: Every trace line (Jobs.java:12, 13, 14, 19, 21, 22, 24) exists and does what the candidate says, and no closing guard appears on the path (src/Jobs.java:13-24), but the only evidence that callbackUrl arrives from a remote POST is the comment at line 12, and the /subscribe route handler is not in the directory, so whether it is reachable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker cannot be verified from this code.
